title: Sections over a quasi-compact open of a directed colimit of sheaves with injective transition maps
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space (sheaves of sets on the site of open subsets of $X$ with open coverings [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]), $I$ a directed set (nonempty, every two elements have a common upper bound), and $(\mathcal F_i,\varphi_{i'i}:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal F_{i'})_{i\le i'}$ a system of sheaves of sets on $X$ over $I$ ($\varphi_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$, $\varphi_{i''i'}\varphi_{i'i}=\varphi_{i''i}$) whose transition maps are injective on sections: $\varphi_{i'i,W}:\mathcal F_i(W)\to\mathcal F_{i'}(W)$ is injective for all $i\le i'$ and all opens $W\subseteq X$. Let $(\mathcal F,(c_i:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal F)_i)$ be a colimit of the system in the category of sheaves of sets on $X$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Then: (1) for every open $W\subseteq X$ and every $i$ the map $c_{i,W}:\mathcal F_i(W)\to\mathcal F(W)$ is injective; (2) if $U\subseteq X$ is a quasi-compact open (every covering of $U$ by open subsets has a finite subcovering), then every $t\in\mathcal F(U)$ is of the form $c_{i,U}(s)$ for some $i\in I$ and $s\in\mathcal F_i(U)$; that is, the canonical map $\varinjlim_i\mathcal F_i(U)\to\mathcal F(U)$ is bijective.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma Tag 009F (lemma-directed-colimits-sections), parts (1) and (3) with their proofs

proof.text: *Step 1 (the colimit is the sheafified presheaf colimit).* Regard $I$ as a category (one arrow $i\to i'$ when $i\le i'$); it is filtered since $I$ is nonempty and directed [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and the system is a functor $i\mapsto\mathcal F_i$ to sheaves of sets on the site $\operatorname{Opens}(X)$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $\mathcal P(V)=\varinjlim_i\mathcal F_i(V)$ with coprojections $\iota_{i,V}$ and restriction maps induced by those of the $\mathcal F_i$ (so $\iota_{i,V}(s)|_{V'}=\iota_{i,V'}(s|_{V'})$ and $\iota_{i',V}\circ\varphi_{i'i,V}=\iota_{i,V}$), and let $\eta:\mathcal P\to\mathcal P^\#$ be its sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. By [lem-weil-pbc-sheaves-colimit-sheafification], $(\mathcal P^\#,(\eta\circ\iota_i)_i)$ is a colimit of the system in sheaves of sets. By uniqueness of colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] there is an isomorphism of sheaves $\theta:\mathcal P^\#\to\mathcal F$ with $\theta\circ\eta\circ\iota_i=c_i$ for all $i$; thus $c_{i,V}=\theta_V\circ\eta_V\circ\iota_{i,V}$ for every open $V$, with $\theta_V$ bijective. Let $\Psi_V:\mathcal P(V)=\varinjlim_i\mathcal F_i(V)\to\mathcal F(V)$ be the canonical map, i.e. the map with $\Psi_V\circ\iota_{i,V}=c_{i,V}$ for all $i$; then $\Psi_V=\theta_V\circ\eta_V$ by the uniqueness in the universal property of the colimit of sets.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma Tag 009F (lemma-directed-colimits-sections), proof of part (1); Section Tag 009E (section-limits-sheaves) item (3)

proof.text: *Step 2 (each $\iota_{i,V}$ is injective and $\mathcal P$ is separated).* Let $V$ be open. If $s,s'\in\mathcal F_i(V)$ and $\iota_{i,V}(s)=\iota_{i,V}(s')$, then by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] (3) there is $i'\ge i$ with $\varphi_{i'i,V}(s)=\varphi_{i'i,V}(s')$, and $\varphi_{i'i,V}$ is injective by hypothesis, so $s=s'$: $\iota_{i,V}$ is injective. Now let $x,y\in\mathcal P(V)$ and let $V=\bigcup_{k\in K}W_k$ be an open covering with $x|_{W_k}=y|_{W_k}$ for all $k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] (1) $x=\iota_{i_1,V}(s_1)$, $y=\iota_{i_2,V}(s_2)$; choosing $i\ge i_1,i_2$ ($I$ directed) and replacing $s_1,s_2$ by $\varphi_{ii_1,V}(s_1),\varphi_{ii_2,V}(s_2)$ we get $x=\iota_{i,V}(s)$, $y=\iota_{i,V}(s')$ with $s,s'\in\mathcal F_i(V)$. Then $\iota_{i,W_k}(s|_{W_k})=x|_{W_k}=y|_{W_k}=\iota_{i,W_k}(s'|_{W_k})$, so $s|_{W_k}=s'|_{W_k}$ by injectivity of $\iota_{i,W_k}$, for every $k$. Since $\mathcal F_i$ is a sheaf on $\operatorname{Opens}(X)$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $\{W_k\to V\}_k$ is a covering, $s=s'$, hence $x=y$. So two sections of $\mathcal P$ that agree on the members of an open covering are equal ($\mathcal P$ is separated; equivalently, in the sense of Stacks, $\mathcal P(V)\to\prod_{x\in V}\mathcal P_x$ is injective, since two sections with the same germs at all points agree on an open covering). No finiteness is used here.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma Tag 009F (lemma-directed-colimits-sections), proof of part (1): the presheaf colimit is separated (Definition Tag 007A, definition-separated) and a separated presheaf injects into its sheafification (Lemma Tag 0082, lemma-separated-presheaf-into-sheaf)

proof.text: *Step 3 (clause (1)).* Let $V$ be open and $p,q\in\mathcal P(V)$ with $\eta_V(p)=\eta_V(q)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] (last clause, for the site $\operatorname{Opens}(X)$, whose coverings are the open coverings) there is an open covering $V=\bigcup_kW_k$ with $p|_{W_k}=q|_{W_k}$ for all $k$, so $p=q$ by Step 2: $\eta_V$ is injective. Hence $c_{i,V}=\theta_V\circ\eta_V\circ\iota_{i,V}$ (Step 1) is a composite of injective maps ($\iota_{i,V}$ by Step 2, $\theta_V$ bijective), so $c_{i,V}$ is injective for every open $V$ and every $i$; this is clause (1). In the same way $\Psi_V=\theta_V\circ\eta_V$ is injective for every open $V$ (Stacks 009F (1)).

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma Tag 009F (lemma-directed-colimits-sections), proof of part (1): the presheaf colimit is separated (Definition Tag 007A, definition-separated) and a separated presheaf injects into its sheafification (Lemma Tag 0082, lemma-separated-presheaf-into-sheaf)

proof.text: *Step 4 (local lifts of a section of $\mathcal F$).* Let $U$ be open and $t\in\mathcal F(U)$, and put $u=\theta_U^{-1}(t)\in\mathcal P^\#(U)$ (Step 1). By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] (first clause) there are an open covering $U=\bigcup_{k\in K}W_k$ and $p_k\in\mathcal P(W_k)$ with $u|_{W_k}=\eta_{W_k}(p_k)$; by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] (1), $p_k=\iota_{i_k,W_k}(s_k)$ with $i_k\in I$ and $s_k\in\mathcal F_{i_k}(W_k)$. As $\theta$ is a morphism of sheaves, $t|_{W_k}=\theta_{W_k}(u|_{W_k})=\theta_{W_k}\eta_{W_k}\iota_{i_k,W_k}(s_k)=c_{i_k,W_k}(s_k)$ (Step 1).

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma Tag 009F (lemma-directed-colimits-sections), proof of part (3)

proof.text: *Step 5 (clause (2): surjectivity over a quasi-compact open, and bijectivity).* Let $U$ be quasi-compact and $t\in\mathcal F(U)$, with $W_k,i_k,s_k$ as in Step 4. Since $U$ is quasi-compact, finitely many $U_1=W_{k_1},\dots,U_m=W_{k_m}$ cover $U$ ($m=0$ when $U=\emptyset$); write $i_j=i_{k_j}$, $s_j=s_{k_j}$. As $I$ is nonempty and directed choose $i\in I$ with $i\ge i_1,\dots,i_m$, and put $\sigma_j=\varphi_{ii_j,U_j}(s_j)\in\mathcal F_i(U_j)$. Since $c_i\circ\varphi_{ii_j}=c_{i_j}$ (the $c$'s form a cocone) and $c_i$ commutes with restriction, $c_{i,U_j}(\sigma_j)=c_{i_j,U_j}(s_j)=t|_{U_j}$; hence for all $j,j'$, $c_{i,U_j\cap U_{j'}}(\sigma_j|_{U_j\cap U_{j'}})=t|_{U_j\cap U_{j'}}=c_{i,U_j\cap U_{j'}}(\sigma_{j'}|_{U_j\cap U_{j'}})$, and by clause (1) (Step 3, injectivity of $c_{i,U_j\cap U_{j'}}$) $\sigma_j$ and $\sigma_{j'}$ agree on $U_j\cap U_{j'}$. By the sheaf property of $\mathcal F_i$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] for the covering $\{U_j\to U\}_{j}$ they glue to $s\in\mathcal F_i(U)$ with $s|_{U_j}=\sigma_j$. Then $c_{i,U}(s)|_{U_j}=c_{i,U_j}(\sigma_j)=t|_{U_j}$ for all $j$, so $c_{i,U}(s)=t$ by the sheaf property of $\mathcal F$. So every $t\in\mathcal F(U)$ is $c_{i,U}(s)=\Psi_U(\iota_{i,U}(s))$: $\Psi_U$ is surjective, and it is injective by Step 3; hence $\varinjlim_i\mathcal F_i(U)\to\mathcal F(U)$ is bijective. (Unlike Stacks 009F (4), no quasi-compactness of $U_j\cap U_{j'}$ is needed: the agreement on overlaps comes from the injectivity of clause (1) at the single index $i$.)
